entries.clue: How you might get thing in a cryptic crossword? (7)

annotation.definition: How you might get thing in a cryptic crossword?

indicatorNotes.cryptic: cryptic means hidden or puzzling, so THING and IN are to be read in a jumbled form

annotation.surface: A question about how a solver is helped towards an answer in a cryptic puzzle.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes itself: you get the answer by hinting, and the letters of THING IN, made cryptic, spell HINTING.
annotation.definitionFit: Crossword clues work by hinting at their answers rather than stating them.

entries.clue: Head of ITV rejected a pitch: 'Love Island Lover' (9)

indicatorNotes.Head of: the head of a word is its top, which in a down clue is its first letter
indicatorNotes.rejected: sent back, so the following pieces are written backwards

annotation.surface: The boss of ITV turns down a pitch for a spin-off of the dating show Love Island.
annotation.walkthrough: Love Island is an ITV reality dating show; here the words split into O and MAN, and pitch is tar, not a sales pitch.
annotation.definitionFit: An Italian loanword: inamorata means a woman with whom one is in love, a sweetheart.

entries.clue: Time Keir reformed accessible transport (5)

indicatorNotes.reformed: formed again, so the letters of KEIR are rearranged

annotation.surface: Prime Minister Keir Starmer's time to reform public transport for disabled people.
annotation.walkthrough: Keir suggests Keir Starmer, the UK prime minister; here it is just four letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A trike, a three-wheeler, is stable and easy to ride, so it is a mobility option.

entries.clue: Band 'Kiss' gets permit (7)

annotation.surface: The rock band Kiss receives a licence.
annotation.walkthrough: Band 'Kiss' reads as the rock group; Band is the definition and Kiss the first piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A necklet is a band worn round the neck.

entries.clue: One's inspired by something comforting in a psalm to find organ (7)

indicatorNotes.inspired by: to be inspired is to be breathed in, so I goes inside the phrase

blocks.note: Psalm 23: 'thy rod and thy staff, they comfort me'
one = I, the Roman numeral; 's = is

annotation.surface: A worshipper takes heart from a comforting psalm and finds an instrument to accompany it.
annotation.walkthrough: The organ of the surface is the church instrument; the answer is the gland in the neck.
annotation.definitionFit: The thyroid is a gland, one of the body's organs.

entries.clue: Petrolhead short of fuel drove one finally for a spin (7)

annotation.definition: Petrolhead short of fuel drove one finally for a spin

indicatorNotes.short of: lacking, so letters are taken away
indicatorNotes.finally: the last letters of fuel, drove and one
indicatorNotes.for a spin: spun round into a new order

blocks.note: last letters of fuel, drove and one, taken out of PETROLHEAD

annotation.surface: A car enthusiast, out of petrol, took one car out for a drive.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a hardtop: a car a petrolhead would take for a spin.
annotation.definitionFit: A hardtop is a car with a rigid roof, just the thing a petrolhead drives for a spin.

entries.clue: One laid down and procreated, wanting love for a change (3,6)

indicatorNotes.wanting: to be wanting something is to lack it, so the O goes
indicatorNotes.for a change: the remaining letters are changed round

annotation.surface: Someone settled down and had children, but the romance has gone.
annotation.walkthrough: One laid down sounds like a person lying down; it is a carpet unrolled for VIPs.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a red carpet is a rug that gets rolled out and laid down for VIPs to walk on.

entries.clue: Occasionally, mind recalls model (5)

indicatorNotes.Occasionally: now and then, so every other letter

blocks.note: the even letters of mInD rEcAlLs

annotation.surface: Now and then the mind remembers a role model.
annotation.walkthrough: Occasionally here means the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on, skipping one each time.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a model pupil is the perfect example, the one to copy.

entries.clue: Change cast: Tarantino must (13)

indicatorNotes.cast: thrown about, as dice or a mould reshapes

annotation.surface: A film casting note: Quentin Tarantino must recast his film.
annotation.walkthrough: Cast looks like a film's cast of actors, which suits Tarantino, but it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: alchemists sought the transmutation of lead into gold, a change of substance.

entries.clue: Country singer broadcast (4)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: something broadcast is heard, not seen, so we go by sound

blocks.note: Bob Marley, the reggae singer; in a non-rhotic British accent the R is silent

annotation.surface: A country-and-western singer goes out on air.
annotation.walkthrough: Country singer reads as a country music star; split it, and Country is the definition while singer is Marley.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Republic of Mali is a landlocked nation in West Africa.

entries.clue: "Dab of cream works on wrinkles" — articles in magazine (10)

indicatorNotes.Dab of: a dab is a small bit, here the first letter of cream
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, placed after what comes before

annotation.surface: A beauty magazine's headline promises a face cream that smooths wrinkles.
annotation.walkthrough: The magazine is not a glossy but the chamber of a gun, which holds cartridges.
annotation.definitionFit: Cartridges are the rounds loaded into a firearm's magazine.

entries.clue: In aircraft, beginning to take Krypton to Superman (4,6)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so take gives T

annotation.surface: Superman flies on an aircraft on his way to Krypton.
annotation.walkthrough: In is not a container signal here; it stands for HOME, as in 'staying in'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Superman was born on Krypton before being sent to Earth as a baby.

entries.clue: Totally posh gaff on Eastenders (3)

annotation.definitionNote: Totally is an adverb; ALL works as one in 'all alone'

indicatorNotes.on Eastenders: EastEnders is a London soap whose Cockney characters drop their Hs

blocks.note: gaff is slang for home; a grand one is a hall
said the Cockney way, HALL loses its H

annotation.surface: A grand house turns up in the soap opera.
annotation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in East London, where the H is dropped: 'ouse for house.
annotation.definitionFit: All means totally, as in 'all wrong'.

entries.clue: Big cat gets man calling ground control (5,3)

annotation.surface: A large cat seems to get a man on the radio to mission control.
annotation.walkthrough: Major Tom is the astronaut of David Bowie's Space Oddity: 'Ground control to Major Tom'.
annotation.definitionFit: Major Tom is the spaceman in radio contact with ground control in Bowie's song.

entries.clue: Nasty old boy with no debts acquiring Twitter now (9)

indicatorNotes.acquiring: to acquire is to take something in, so NO IOUS takes X into itself

blocks.note: NO + IOUS, written promises to pay

annotation.surface: A former pupil, debt-free, becomes a nasty presence on social media.
annotation.walkthrough: An IOU is a written promise to repay a debt; Twitter was renamed X in 2023, and the new name slots between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an obnoxious person is offensively unpleasant, which is what nasty describes.

entries.clue: Successor to Oscar Wilde staging primarily juicy stuff (6)

indicatorNotes.Successor to: the word that comes after Oscar in the NATO alphabet
indicatorNotes.primarily: first, so the first letters of Wilde and staging

blocks.note: O is Oscar and P is Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
first letters of Wilde and staging

annotation.surface: A dramatist who follows Oscar Wilde stages racy, juicy material.
annotation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde suggests a playwright; the solver only needs the NATO alphabet, where Papa follows Oscar.
annotation.definitionFit: Papaws, or papayas, are juicy tropical fruit.

entries.clue: Online influencer's woke, wanting content Mr Beast put out (9)

indicatorNotes.wanting content: without its inside letters, so woke becomes WE
indicatorNotes.put out: displaced, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A social media star is woke, disliking what the YouTuber MrBeast posts.
annotation.walkthrough: MrBeast is a hugely popular YouTuber, fitting online influencer; his name is just letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A webmaster runs a website and so controls what appears on it online.

entries.clue: Some mountain ranges around magical land (6)

indicatorNotes.Some: only part of the words is used

blocks.note: the letters sit across the join: mount(AIN RAN)ges

annotation.surface: Mountain ranges encircle an enchanted realm.
annotation.walkthrough: Read mountAIN RANges backwards to find the land.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: C S Lewis's children reach an enchanted kingdom of talking animals through a wardrobe.

entries.clue: Bit of moussaka spilling in space to stay (7)

indicatorNotes.spilling: what spills out of a container is lost from it, so IN drops out of AUBERGINE

blocks.note: aubergine, or eggplant, is a main ingredient of moussaka
these letters spill out of AUBERGINE

annotation.surface: Some moussaka falls on the floor in a place where you are staying.
annotation.walkthrough: In reads as a preposition; it is the two letters that fall out.
annotation.definitionFit: A French loanword: an auberge is a country inn, somewhere travellers put up for the night.

entries.clue: Try piece of rigatoni as part of experiment (4,4)

annotation.surface: A cook samples a piece of pasta as part of a culinary trial.
annotation.walkthrough: Piece of rigatoni looks like a first-letter signal, but it is a whole piece: one tube of pasta.
annotation.definitionFit: A test tube is standard glassware in a laboratory experiment.

entries.clue: One listing characters: Harry, Ron, or Hermione? (7)

blocks.note: one who spells out a word letter by letter

annotation.surface: Someone lists the characters in Harry Potter.
annotation.walkthrough: Characters means letters, not people in a story; the question mark flags the jokey second sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A speller names letters in order; Harry Potter's wizards are casters of spells.

entries.clue: Quince moved from Madrid to Rome, swallowing European lies about bug (3)

indicatorNotes.moved from Madrid to Rome: Quince, Spanish for fifteen, is written the Roman way as XV
indicatorNotes.swallowing: what is swallowed ends up inside, so XV takes E into its middle
indicatorNotes.about: to turn about is to face the other way, so XEV is read backwards

blocks.clueFragment: Quince moved from Madrid to Rome
blocks.note: quince is Spanish for fifteen; in Roman numerals XV

annotation.surface: The setter Quince travels from Spain to Italy and tells tall tales about an insect.
annotation.walkthrough: Quince is the setter's own pseudonym and a fruit, but read as Spanish it is the number fifteen.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to annoy or irritate someone persistently.

entries.clue: Hate one about to feed five thousand (5)

indicatorNotes.about: to turn about is to face the other way, so ONE is read backwards
indicatorNotes.to feed: put into the mouth of V M

annotation.surface: Resentment at being the one sent to feed the five thousand.
annotation.walkthrough: Feeding the five thousand is the Gospel miracle; here five thousand is V and M, not 5000.
annotation.definitionFit: Venom is bitter hatred or spite.

entries.clue: Pulse from bachelor, say, began after heart bypass (10)

indicatorNotes.heart bypass: the heart of began is skipped over

blocks.note: BEGAN without its middle letter G

annotation.surface: A single man's pulse picks up after heart surgery.
annotation.walkthrough: Pulse and heart set up a medical story; a pulse is also a legume, and bachelor, say is two pieces, not a noun and its example.
annotation.definitionFit: The butter bean is a large pale bean, one of the pulses.

entries.clue: Fed up with views shifting to the right on computer (5)

indicators: shifting to the right on computer

indicatorNotes.shifting to the right on computer: each letter moves one key to the right on a QWERTY keyboard

blocks.clueFragment: shifting to the right on computer
blocks.note: V to B, I to O, E to R, W to E, S to D on the keyboard

annotation.surface: Tired of changing opinions leaning rightwards on the internet.
annotation.walkthrough: Shifting to the right sounds political; on a keyboard, each letter of VIEWS sits just left of a letter of BORED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone fed up with something has had enough of it, which is to be bored with it.

entries.clue: Hotel offering party after trendy men ring back (6,4)

indicatorNotes.after: coming after means placed later, so DO is written behind IN

blocks.note: other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

annotation.surface: A hotel hosts a party for fashionable men who promise to call back.
annotation.walkthrough: Hotel offering reads as a verb phrase, but it is a noun: something a hotel offers.
annotation.definitionFit: An indoor pool is a facility many hotels offer guests.

entries.clue: Sun set to the west - how disappointing (4)

indicatorNotes.set to the west: in an across clue, west is leftward, so the word runs right to left

annotation.surface: The sun sinks in the west, and someone sighs at the view.
annotation.walkthrough: The sun really does set in the west, which disguises the instruction to write STAR backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'Rats!' is what you exclaim when something goes wrong, so it stands for 'how disappointing'.

entries.clue: Entrance to sacred ground in pieces (7)

indicatorNotes.Entrance to: the way in, the first letter of sacred

annotation.surface: A gateway to holy ground lies in ruins.
annotation.walkthrough: Sacred ground wants to be read together; split them, and ground is a verb meaning crushed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a vase that has been shattered lies in pieces.

entries.clue: Dealers arrested in order to get rid of ecstasy (7)

indicatorNotes.in order: the letters are put in order, that is, arranged afresh
indicatorNotes.to get rid of: to get rid of something is to throw it out, so E leaves ARRESTED

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy; one E is taken out

annotation.surface: Drug dealers are arrested in order to get ecstasy off the streets.
annotation.walkthrough: Dealers suggests drug dealers; they are just traders.
annotation.definitionFit: Dealers and traders both buy and sell.
